title: Closure under the tensor-power reflections makes a tensor set into a Cartan graph

statement_spans.label: author Proposition environment, source label RdGraph (statement, source lines 747-753)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following it (source lines 754-770)

standard_prerequisites: Cartan graphs: a quadruple (I, A, (rho_i), (c^q)) with finite index set I, set of objects A, reflections rho_i, and generalized Cartan matrices c^q, satisfying axioms (C1) and (C2) (source Section 3 definitions).

The tensor-power construction of Section 3: for a tensor q in K^{I^dn} with defined Cartan matrix c^q, the reflection operator sigma^q_l and its eigenvectors v_m, w_m, s_m with the eigenvalue relations (sigma^q_l)^{tensor dn}(v_m) = v_m, (w_m) -> -w_m, (s_m) -> s_m (source Section 3.2, recalled inside the proof at lines 762-764).

The factorization Rossod (3.8) of the condition R_m = 0 as (1 - bich_q(v_m))(1 - bich_q(w_m))/(1 - chi_q(s_m)), restated inside the proof at line 761, and Theorem cartan_d (3.7) stating that c^q is a generalized Cartan matrix.
core_obligations: Let dn in N be even, I = {1, ..., n}, and A a set of tensors q in K^{I^dn} with defined Cartan matrix c^q. Assume that for all q in A and l in I the reflection rho_l(q) := sigma^q_l(q) again lies in A. Then (I, A, (rho_i)_{i in I}, (c^q)_{q in A}) is a Cartan graph.
proof_roadmap: Axiom (C1) part: the matrices c^q are generalized Cartan matrices by Proposition RdCartan (3.8) (line 756).

Axiom (C1) closure part: if (C2) holds then (C1) holds as well, because rho_l is defined by a reflection of order two and sigma^q_l = sigma^{rho_l(q)}_l since the relevant Cartan entries agree by (C2) (line 757).

Axiom (C2): compare c^q_{l,j} and c^{rho_l(q)}_{l,j} for l != j (line 759). With m := -c^q_{l,j} one has R_m = 0 and R_k != 0 for k < m; insert the factorization R_m = (1 - bich_q(v_m))(1 - bich_q(w_m))/(1 - chi_q(s_m)) (line 761) and use the eigenvector relations for v_m, w_m, s_m under (sigma^q_l)^{tensor dn} (lines 762-764): replacing q by sigma^q_l(q) sends the second factor to (1 - bich_q(-w_m)), which vanishes exactly when w_m = 0 (lines 765-767).

Close via the definition of the Cartan entries through the vanishing of the R_k (eqref cartan_d, line 768): the new condition produces the same Cartan entry c^q_{l,j} = c^{rho_l(q)}_{l,j} for l != j, establishing (C2), and with it the Cartan graph property.
